bio: 22 • Greenhouse botanist  Researching subtropical epiphytes by day, taking care of a very old glasshouse by night. I like curious people, quiet places, and anyone who can survive a little dirt on their shoes.

choices.choiceText: I have a few quiet survivors on my windowsill. Jade and trailing pothos.
I'm the kind of person who manages to kill low-maintenance succulents.
Okay, but before the plant interrogation... what are you actually like?
Plants are fine, but I'm swiping on you, not a potted fern.
Honestly? They just make a mess with dirt and dead leaves.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Jade and pothos are good choices. They're pretty forgiving, which I respect. Give them decent light, don't drown them, and they usually cooperate.

I see so many people buy a fancy Monstera for the photos and then panic the second a leaf goes weird. What made you keep yours around?

choices.choiceText: Having something quiet and alive around keeps me grounded when life gets loud.
Watching a new leaf open after a rough week is weirdly comforting.
Someone gave them to me, and honestly I felt too guilty to let them die.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Honestly, 'black thumb' usually means somebody watered the poor thing to death. Succulents are weird like that. People think they're helping, then the roots just sit in wet soil and give up.

Half the time it's not neglect. It's too much love in the wrong direction.

choices.choiceText: Too much love can still be suffocating. That sounds dangerously like relationships.
Okay, teach me. How do I stop killing them with good intentions?
I may have forgotten mine existed for three weeks on a dark bookshelf.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Fair. But the greenhouse really is a huge part of my life. It's where I go when I need to breathe.

So if someone hates the smell of soil or gets annoyed when I have dirt on my sleeves... we'd probably run out of things to talk about pretty fast.

choices.choiceText: Damp wood and clean earth smell a hundred times better than city fumes. Tell me about your sanctuary.
I don't mind soil. I just wanted to make sure there was a person behind the greenery.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Dirt's kind of the point, {PlayerName}. It's messy, but it's where all the interesting stuff happens.

So yeah, if you need everything spotless all the time, my world might drive you a little nuts.

choices.choiceText: Okay, I was being blunt. So why does that 'mess' matter so much to you?
I just like clean floors. I'm not built for an indoor jungle.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Yeah. Grounded is exactly the word. Everything moves so fast now—messages, deadlines, people. Plants don't care about any of that.

You sit there watching a new leaf grow and suddenly you're not thinking about your phone anymore. It's hard not to slow down with them.

choices.choiceText: Was that part of why you got into botany in the first place?
Honestly, my pulse slows down when I'm talking to someone who actually listens. Like you.

nodes.partnerMessage:
I love watching a new leaf come out. At first it's all tightly folded, then over a day or two it slowly opens up.

It's such a small thing, but you actually have to slow down enough to notice it. Most people never do.

choices.choiceText: Patience is underrated. What are you studying right now?
I'd rather wait for a leaf with you than sit in traffic for ten minutes.

nodes.partnerMessage: That's how it starts! You feel bad for one sad little plant at a clearance sale, and suddenly two years later you're living in a jungle.

choices.choiceText: Does your personal place look like a Jurassic conservatory?

nodes.partnerMessage:
...Okay, that's actually a really good comparison.

People can do that too, I think. They get scared of losing someone, so they hold on tighter and tighter until neither person can breathe. Roots need air too.

You notice more than I expected you to.

choices.choiceText: I believe in giving people room to grow. You included.
Do people in your life tend to crowd you?

nodes.partnerMessage:
Rule one: use an unglazed terra cotta pot when the plant likes to dry out a little. The clay helps with that.

Rule two: pick up the pot before you water. If it's still heavy, leave it alone.

Seriously, feeling the weight tells you more than people think.

choices.choiceText: 'Feel the weight before you act.' You really turn everything into life advice, huh?
Okay. What's rule three?

nodes.partnerMessage:
Three weeks?!  That plant was probably trying to escape through the hallway.

Okay, we're having an intervention for your houseplants. I don't make the rules.

choices.choiceText: Okay, fair. What's the rehab plan?

nodes.partnerMessage:
It's the university's old 19th-century palm house. Huge iron arches, glass panels that fog up when the misters run, and a little water-lily pool where a bullfrog somehow lives year-round.

Once the gates close at night, it gets ridiculously quiet. You barely hear the city anymore.

choices.choiceText: That sounds kind of beautiful, actually. Like a little glass world in the middle of the city.
Do you really stay there alone after hours?

nodes.partnerMessage:
There is definitely a person. She just happens to spend a lot of time talking to pitcher plants because they don't interrupt or drag her into networking events.

I know I can be a little guarded. I think you get that way when you've spent a long time protecting things you care about.

choices.choiceText: You don't have to apologize for protecting your peace. I respect it.
Pitcher plants are bad listeners, though. What's actually on your mind tonight?

nodes.partnerMessage:
Because nature is messy on purpose. Leaves fall, they break down, the soil gets fed, and something new grows from it.

That's why I'm not bothered by a little mess. Sometimes the stuff that looks dead is exactly what makes room for the next thing.

choices.choiceText: That's actually a really gentle way to look at decay and recovery.
Where did that way of looking at things come from?

nodes.partnerMessage:
Then we're probably not a great match, {PlayerName}. 

I work with living soil. There will be compost on my boots. I'm not apologizing for that.

choices.choiceText: Wait, Masie. That came out wrong. I didn't mean to insult what you do.
Whatever. Have fun with your compost.

nodes.partnerMessage:
My grandmother had a tiny greenhouse behind her old brick house. We'd sit in there during storms while the rain hit the glass and she'd make mint tea from the garden.

She died when I was sixteen, but every now and then the greenhouse smells exactly like hers. It's strange how fast that can bring a memory back.

choices.choiceText: You're carrying a piece of her with you through all this. That's really beautiful.
Do you still make tea the way she did?

nodes.partnerMessage:
...Okay, you're making me blush. That's embarrassing. 

I'm supposed to be the calm science person here, not the one getting flustered over a dating app message.

choices.choiceText: Even scientists deserve to feel their heart skip a beat occasionally.
What's the specimen on your workbench right now?

nodes.partnerMessage:
A little colony of *Drosera spatulata*—spoon-leaved sundews. They're tiny, covered in those sticky hairs that catch insects, and they sparkle like little red jewels under good light.

Pretty cute until you're a fruit fly, obviously.

choices.choiceText: Quiet girl, carnivorous plants... there's a little wild side to you, huh?
I've always liked carnivorous plants. Do you actually feed them yourself?

nodes.partnerMessage: You're really choosing plants over rush hour? I might have to make you an honorary botanist. I'll even find you an apron.

choices.choiceText: I'll wear the apron if you pour the tea. Tell me about your tea blends.

nodes.partnerMessage:
My apartment has more grow lights than actual lamps. 

My roommate keeps joking that anyone looking through the windows would assume we're running some illegal operation. It's literally just a pile of Philodendrons trying not to die.

choices.choiceText: Thirty rare Philodendrons and a grow-op misunderstanding. I love that so much.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Thank you, {PlayerName}. Honestly, that's a really good thing to hear.

I don't need someone hovering over me to prove they care. I just want someone who can be close without making me feel trapped.

choices.choiceText: I'll always give you room to breathe, Masie. Tell me about your evening in the glasshouse.

nodes.partnerMessage:
My family had a pretty specific plan for me. Pre-med, stable career, nice house, the whole thing.

Then I switched into plant biology and started working nights in the conservatory. They took it really personally.

They wanted a neat little hedge. I wanted the whole forest.

choices.choiceText: Clipped hedges are boring and sterile. Overgrown forests are where real life lives.
It takes guts to stop living the life someone else picked for you.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Gardening absolutely counts as life advice. Plants have been figuring out how to survive for way longer than we have.

Honestly, I think we'd have fewer problems if people learned when to water, when to wait, and when to let something go.

choices.choiceText: Then teach me. Where do I get more of this plant wisdom?

nodes.partnerMessage:
Rule three: prune when you need to. If a part of the plant is done, keeping it there doesn't magically bring it back.

People are weirdly bad at accepting that lesson for themselves.

choices.choiceText: Okay, that's a hard lesson, but I get it.

nodes.partnerMessage:
First, we move the survivor somewhere with decent morning light. Then we check the roots and repot it properly.

And yes, I'm supervising you. I don't trust you near a succulent unsupervised anymore.

choices.choiceText: I'm ready for strict supervision, botanist.

nodes.partnerMessage:
That's exactly what it feels like. At dusk, the outside lights hit the condensation on the glass and everything gets this soft green glow.

I'll sit by the pond with tea and just watch the water for a while. It's probably the closest thing I have to an off switch.

choices.choiceText: I can picture you sitting by that stone pond so vividly. It sounds magical.
Is there room on that stone pond bench for two people?

nodes.partnerMessage:
Most nights, yeah. My shift ends around 7:30, but I usually stay a couple more hours.

There's a little wooden bench behind the bog display where I do notes and sketches. It's quiet back there—just the pumps and the occasional drip from the glass.

choices.choiceText: You sketch your specimens? You're an artist as well as a scientist.
Does it ever get lonely in there after dark?

nodes.partnerMessage:
Thanks. Dating apps make everything feel so rushed sometimes. Five messages in and people already want to know your entire life story.

I like that you're letting this be a conversation instead of a race.

choices.choiceText: Plants don't rush their bloom. Neither will I.
So what are you working on tonight?

nodes.partnerMessage:
I've been thinking about winter dormancy lately. Plants basically give themselves permission to slow down when they need to.

People aren't nearly as good at that. We keep pushing and then act surprised when we're exhausted.

choices.choiceText: I think people could learn from that. Are you burned out right now?

nodes.partnerMessage:
I think that's part of why the greenhouse helped after my grandmother died. Nothing there really disappears cleanly. Things break down, feed the soil, and eventually something else grows.

It didn't make losing her easier, but it gave me a way to understand it.

choices.choiceText: She taught you something profound that outlived her. That's true immortality.

nodes.partnerMessage:
...I appreciate the apology. I get defensive about this stuff because people sometimes act like my work is just watering plants and getting dirty.

So if you're actually curious about why it matters to me, I'm happy to keep talking.

choices.choiceText: I am. Show me what's on your workbench tonight, Masie.

nodes.partnerMessage: I will. Have fun in your sterile hallway.

Thank you, {PlayerName}. That one hit me a little.

I actually keep a cutting from her old Christmas cactus on my lab bench. It's been growing for decades now. Every December it still puts out these ridiculous magenta flowers.

choices.choiceText: Forty-four years old... that plant is living family history.
Okay, now I need to see this cactus blooming.

nodes.partnerMessage:
I do. Spearmint, lemon verbena, a little chamomile, sometimes stevia leaf. Nothing fancy.

It makes a really good tea, though. And yes, if you ever visit, I'll make you a mug.

choices.choiceText: Tea in your greenhouse with rain hitting the glass? That's a pretty good date to me.
I'm holding you to that tea promise.

nodes.partnerMessage:
You're trouble, {PlayerName}. 

I usually have my composure together, and now I'm sitting here rereading your messages like an idiot. Let's talk about plants before I embarrass myself.

choices.choiceText: Okay, now I'm curious. What was the reckless thing you almost said?
Tell me about the sundews before you get me in trouble.

nodes.partnerMessage:
People confuse quiet with harmless all the time. Just because I don't talk loudly doesn't mean I can't be stubborn.

Sundews are basically proof. They look sweet and sparkly, then they digest insects.

choices.choiceText: I'd never underestimate you. Quiet doesn't mean weak.
I like a little attitude. Keeps things interesting.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Distilled rainwater only. Tap water can be too mineral-heavy for them.

And when bugs are scarce in winter, yes, I sometimes feed them tiny bits of rehydrated bloodworms with tweezers. It sounds ridiculous until you've spent six hours taking care of them.

choices.choiceText: You actually feed them with tweezers? That's kind of adorable dedication.

nodes.partnerMessage:
We actually had campus security knock once because the purple glow from our apartment windows looked suspicious from across the quad. 

He came in, saw the plants, laughed, and asked if we had a Monstera cutting for his wife.

choices.choiceText: Hahaha. Plant cuttings as a peace offering is actually genius.

nodes.partnerMessage:
An overgrown forest, yeah. Moss everywhere, roots doing whatever they want, nothing trimmed just to make it look tidy.

My family has never really understood why I love that. So... it means something that you get it.

choices.choiceText: You don't have to explain it. I get you, forest and all.

nodes.partnerMessage:
It was terrifying, honestly. I was nineteen, packing up my botanical books while my mom was telling me I was throwing away my earning potential.

But every time I look around the glasshouse at night, I remember that I chose this life for myself.

choices.choiceText: And you built a life of real substance. That's worth more than any corporate title.

nodes.partnerMessage:
This app is kind of a terrible place for actual conversations. Everything feels like you're supposed to be witty in one sentence and then swipe again.

I keep a quieter little journal on Line with my night notes, plant photos, and sketches. It's more my speed.

choices.choiceText: Give me the greenhouse key. I want to read your night notes.

nodes.partnerMessage:
It is. Even when you know something is over, cutting it off can still hurt.

I've had to do that with people too—walk away from relationships where I was constantly being pushed into a version of myself that wasn't really me. It sucked, but eventually life got healthier.

choices.choiceText: I'm honored that you're letting me be part of the healthy new growth.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Strict supervision, then. If I catch you using a plastic moisture meter before you've even picked up the pot, you're on peat-tray duty. 

...I might let you have some tea, though.

choices.choiceText: Tea after potting lessons sounds pretty perfect. Let's go somewhere quieter.

nodes.partnerMessage:
It feels like stepping out of normal life for a couple of hours. The lilies close up, everything gets quiet, and you stop checking what time it is.

It's probably the only place where I genuinely forget about my phone.

choices.choiceText: I want to share that peace with you, Masie.

nodes.partnerMessage:
There's room. The bench gets freezing at night, though.

So... you'd probably have to sit pretty close if you wanted to stay warm.

choices.choiceText: I don't mind sitting close. Show me the private feed.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Yeah, mostly graphite and sepia watercolor. Photos are useful, but drawing something by hand makes you notice details you would otherwise miss.

You can't really fake a sketch. You have to understand what you're looking at.

choices.choiceText: I'd love to see the sketches. Can you show me?

nodes.partnerMessage:
Sometimes. Especially when the fans shut off and all you can hear is water dripping from the glass.

I like being alone, but every now and then I look at the empty bench by the pond and think it'd be nice to have someone sitting there with me.

choices.choiceText: You don't have to sit by that pond alone. I'm here.

nodes.partnerMessage:
...Okay. I'm screenshotting that.

I don't think anyone on this app has talked to me quite like that before. I like the idea of not having to rush this.

choices.choiceText: You deserve gentleness, Masie. Always. Let's move somewhere quieter to talk.

nodes.partnerMessage:
A little, yeah.

Between grant work, thesis data, and trying to keep a few hundred living specimens happy across different rooms, I've been running on fumes.

Talking to you is actually the first time all week I've felt like I could sit down and just breathe.

choices.choiceText: Drop your shoulders. Breathe. I'll keep you company.

nodes.partnerMessage:
It really is. I usually root a couple of cuttings from it every spring.

When I give one to a friend, I always say, 'You're holding a little piece of my family history, so please don't murder it.'

choices.choiceText: Would you trust me with one of those cuttings?

nodes.partnerMessage:
I have photos of it blooming under the lab lights. The flowers are this ridiculous neon magenta.

I put the full album in my private greenhouse feed if you want to see it properly.

choices.choiceText: Show me the album. Send the link.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Tea, rain hitting the glass, warm bread... honestly, that's a pretty good date.

Show up like that one evening and I might even trust you with a greenhouse key.

choices.choiceText: I'll bring bread. Now give me the private link.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Okay, promise made. Two mugs, fresh mint tea, and no random dating-app nonsense.

Let's take this somewhere quieter.

choices.choiceText: Lead the way, Masie.

nodes.partnerMessage:
...I haven't actually looked forward to seeing a message this much in a long time.

Which is a little embarrassing to admit. So before I lose my nerve, let's move somewhere quieter.

choices.choiceText: Okay, send me the invite.

nodes.partnerMessage:
You notice little things. I like that about you.

It's making me want to show you more of my world than I normally would this early.

choices.choiceText: Show me. I want to see your world.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Careful. You might actually end up in the carnivorous bog room feeding sundews with tweezers on a Friday night. 

Let's see if you're still this confident in my private feed.

choices.choiceText: I'm ready. Lead the way.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Thank you. I don't really see it as a chore. These plants depend on me, and I like knowing I've helped them make it to another season.

I have some lab sketches and night-bloom photos I'd rather show you somewhere the app won't turn them into blurry thumbnails.

choices.choiceText: Send me the private link. I want to see them properly.

nodes.partnerMessage:
It works every time. Botanists have our own weird little currency. 

We've also been talking on this app for way too long, so come find me in the private feed.

choices.choiceText: Okay, joining your private room now.

nodes.partnerMessage:
...Okay, 'forest and all' actually got me.

I'm locking up the bench now. Come talk to me in the private feed where we can actually slow down a little.

choices.choiceText: Opening the door. I'm coming in.

nodes.partnerMessage:
It's honestly nice having someone say that. I don't hear it very often.

Come over to my private room on Line. I want to show you something I've been working on.

choices.choiceText: I'm on my way.

nodes.partnerMessage:
I think you already are. Talking to you feels easy, which is weirdly rare on here.

Come to my private greenhouse room. We can leave the swipe-app chaos behind.

choices.choiceText: Leaving the crowd behind. See you there.

nodes.partnerMessage:
I'd like that. It's getting late, and I usually stop checking this app around now anyway.

I keep my field notes and sketches in a quieter room on Line. I'll show you there.

choices.choiceText: Got the link. See you there.

nodes.partnerMessage:
...Okay, you got me.

I'm sitting here by the pond with my phone against my chest, and I didn't realize how badly I wanted to hear that.

Come find me in the private feed.

choices.choiceText: Right there with you by the pond.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Shoulders actually dropped. That helped.

Thank you, {PlayerName}. Come over to the private feed. I think I want to keep talking to you without all the noise.

choices.choiceText: I'm heading into your private feed now.

nodes.partnerMessage:
I think I would. But I'm inspecting your potting technique in person first, so don't get too excited. 

Come over to my private feed and we'll plan it.

choices.choiceText: Okay, planning my visit now.

nodes.partnerMessage:
I just opened my private greenhouse room. Better photos, my actual field notes, sketches, and none of the swipe-app noise.

Come in, {PlayerName}. Stay a while.
Okay, enough about plants for one second. What are you actually like when you're not trying to sound impressive on a dating app?

choices.choiceText: Mostly tired, hungry, and pretending I have my life together.
I was hoping you'd ask. I'm probably less impressive than my profile suggests.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Good. That's probably more believable anyway. 

I'm not exactly glamorous either. Today I spent twenty minutes looking for my pruning shears while they were literally in my hand.

choices.choiceText: Okay, that actually makes you feel more human.
So you're saying the intimidating botanist thing is fake?

nodes.partnerMessage:
Excuse me. The botanist thing is very real. The intimidating part is still under review.

I'm just... less polished than I probably sound on here.

choices.choiceText: Good. I'd rather talk to the real you anyway.

nodes.partnerMessage:
That's probably the nicest thing you could say to me this early.

Okay. Now I'm curious about you again.

choices.choiceText: Ask me something you actually want to know.

nodes.partnerMessage:
What's something small that can instantly make a bad day better for you?

Mine is tea in the greenhouse when it rains. And, apparently, talking to you now.

choices.choiceText: Honestly? A good conversation and not having to pretend I'm fine.
Food. I'm very easy to bribe with good food.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Then we're probably going to get along. I don't need everything to be impressive either.

Sometimes I just want a quiet room and one person I can be myself around.

choices.choiceText: That sounds pretty close to what I want too.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Useful information. We can work with food. 

I make decent tea, but my actual cooking skills are questionable. I once burnt soup so badly the kitchen smelled like pennies for two days.

choices.choiceText: Then I'll handle the food, you handle the plants.
